::: {#sol-squares-zero}

**If $x = 0$ and $y = 0$, then $x^2 + y^2 = 0$.**
Suppose $x = 0$ and $y = 0$.
Then $x^2 + y^2 = 0^2 + 0^2 = 0$.

**If $x^2 + y^2 = 0$, then $x = 0$ and $y = 0$.**
Suppose $x^2 + y^2 = 0$.
A square of a real number is never negative, so $y^2 \ge 0$, and

$$
\ba
x^2
&= -y^2
&& \text{(subtract } y^2 \text{ from both sides of } x^2 + y^2 = 0 \text{)}
\\&\le 0.
&& \text{(} y^2 \ge 0 \text{)}
\ea
$$

Also $x^2 \ge 0$, so $x^2 = 0$, and so $x = 0$.
The same steps with $x$ and $y$ swapped give $y = 0$.

:::
